solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Artist is in shock with valuation (9)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in' places the artist and 'is' inside the word for shock, splitting it open

annotation.surface: A painter reels at what an expert says the work is worth.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shock' looks like the painter's feeling on hearing the price; it is a verb, and 'is' is simply itself.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an expert's estimate of what a painting or house is worth.

entries.clue: Keen to get on circuit with promises of money (9)

indicatorNotes.with: 'with' means accompanied by, so the promises of money come along after the circuit

blocks.note: an ambit is a circuit or compass
IOUs are written promises to pay

annotation.surface: A salesman eager to get on the road, promising money to all.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is the whole phrase 'Keen to get on', meaning eager to advance, not just 'Keen'.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: to 'get on' is to advance in life, and being keen for that is the whole meaning.

entries.clue: Presentation for each class with master introducing Newton (11)

indicatorNotes.introducing: to introduce is to bring in, so the master brings Newton inside itself

blocks.note: per = for each, as in 'per head'
a form is a school class
an ace is a master of a skill
N is the symbol for the newton, the unit of force

annotation.surface: A school prize-giving where each class and its teacher present something about Isaac Newton.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Master' looks like a schoolmaster in this classroom scene; it means an expert. A form is a class in a British school.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a play or concert put on before an audience is a presentation.

entries.clue: Fool around near pit (5)

indicatorNotes.around: 'around' puts the fool on both sides of the word for near

blocks.note: by = near, as in 'stand by me'

annotation.surface: Someone messing about dangerously close to the edge of a mine shaft.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fool around' reads as one phrase, to mess about; split it, and 'around' is the instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a bottomless-seeming chasm is a pit.

entries.clue: Guest called in endlessly demanding (8)

indicatorNotes.in: 'called in' reads as one phrase, but 'in' alone sends the call inside the other word
indicatorNotes.endlessly: without an end, so the last letter goes

annotation.surface: A visitor summoned indoors who keeps making demands.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Called in' reads as a phrasal verb; split it into the phone call and the container instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: An older sense: a visitor to a house was a stranger, as in 'you're quite a stranger'.

entries.clue: Need a moment talking about newborn’s nourishment? (6)

indicatorNotes.talking: in talking the words are spoken, so we go by their sound, not their spelling

blocks.note: a tick is a moment, as in 'just a tick'

annotation.surface: A new parent asking for a minute while talking about the baby's feeding.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is an adjective phrase: milk is a newborn's food, hence the question mark on a definition by example.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the word means relating to milk, and milk is what a newborn lives on.

entries.clue: Plant thyme with March sun about (13)

indicatorNotes.about: 'about' means scattered around, so the letters are moved about

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 13 letters; 'with' joins the words

annotation.surface: Gardening advice: put in the thyme when the March sun comes out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Plant' reads as a verb in a gardening tip; it is the noun, the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the answer is one kind of flowering plant.

entries.clue: Hero of Conan Doyle’s ill-fated craft (10)

blocks.note: the professor who leads the expedition in The Lost World
the space shuttle that broke apart after launch in 1986

annotation.surface: A question about a doomed vessel in one of Arthur Conan Doyle's stories.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface joins the two halves, as if the craft belonged to Conan Doyle; they are separate things that share a name. Professor Challenger is his other hero, after Holmes.
annotation.definitionFit: Two proper names: Professor Challenger of The Lost World, and the shuttle Challenger lost in 1986.

entries.clue: Note sections of family into baroque restoration (12)

indicatorNotes.baroque: baroque means extravagantly odd, so the letters of 'into' are twisted out of order

blocks.note: re (ray) is the second note of the sol-fa scale
in biology a family is divided into genera

annotation.surface: Advice on restoring a baroque building, with a family's history in mind.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Family' is the biological rank, not relatives. 'Into' looks like a link word; it is the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: renewal of something decayed, as of a run-down town centre.

entries.clue: Relative’s place accommodating papa and daughter (7)

indicatorNotes.accommodating: to accommodate is to give lodging, so the place takes the papa and daughter in

blocks.note: stead = place, as in 'in his stead'
Papa is P in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: A family member's house putting up a father and his daughter.
annotation.walkthrough: The family setting makes papa look like the father here; it is the NATO letter P, and the actual father is the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a relative by marriage, the mother's new husband.

entries.clue: Like some subs round place were destroyed (7-7)

indicatorNotes.destroyed: what is destroyed is broken up, and its letters are rebuilt

annotation.surface: Submarines that circled a town, which was then wiped out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Round' reads as the preposition, about a place; it is just five letters of fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: many naval submarines run on a reactor.

entries.clue: Hot and really intense spicy sauce, African originally (7)

annotation.definition: Hot and really intense spicy sauce, African originally

indicatorNotes.originally: take the origin, the first letter, of each word

blocks.clueFragment: Hot and really intense spicy sauce, African
blocks.note: first letters of Hot And Really Intense Spicy Sauce African

annotation.surface: A description of a fiery North African chilli paste.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue both spells the answer and describes it, so there is no separate definition to find.
annotation.definitionFit: An &lit: the whole clue describes the hot chilli paste of North Africa.

entries.clue: Unsocial person Martin hopes to get thrown out (11)

indicatorNotes.to get thrown out: what is thrown out lands in disorder, and so do the letters

annotation.surface: A loner named Martin who wants to be kicked out of a club.
annotation.walkthrough: Someone who dislikes people would indeed welcome being thrown out, so the surface fits the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone who dislikes and avoids other people.

entries.clue: Salad dressing, month old (4)

blocks.note: O = old, as in OT for Old Testament

annotation.surface: A jar of mayonnaise found to be a month past its date.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a fridge check; the month and 'old' are just letters.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal short form of mayonnaise, a common salad dressing.

entries.clue: Stout is left in sink (5)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in sink' sets the scene, but 'in' also puts left inside the word for sink

blocks.note: to sink something deep is to bury it

annotation.surface: A pint of stout abandoned in the kitchen sink.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stout' is set up as the beer left in the sink; it is the adjective, meaning heavily built.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, of a person: big and heavily built.

entries.clue: Oblong area for games with mat (9)

indicatorNotes.with: 'with' means alongside, so the mat follows the games area

blocks.note: a rec is a recreation ground, a public playing field
to mat, as hair does, is to tangle

annotation.surface: A rectangular sports ground laid with a mat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mat' is a verb here, what hair does, not a floor covering. A rec is British for a public playing field.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a four-sided shape longer than it is wide.

entries.clue: Bow you once nearly hit when reversing (7)

indicatorNotes.nearly: nearly, not quite, so the last letter is dropped
indicatorNotes.when reversing: reversing is backing up, so the whole string is read backwards

blocks.note: ye is the old form of you

annotation.surface: A driver who almost knocked someone down while backing up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bow' could be a ship's front or an archer's weapon; here it is the greeting, the woman's form made by bending the knees.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the bob of the knees made in greeting, the counterpart of a man's bow.

entries.clue: Things ruin sodden salads — this could be one of them (8,6,8)

annotation.definition: Things ruin sodden salads — this could be one of them

indicatorNotes.could be: the letters could be rearranged into the answer

annotation.surface: A complaint that some things spoil a soggy salad, with a suggestion of which.
annotation.walkthrough: The first four words are both the fodder and the complaint: a heavy dressing is one thing that leaves salads sodden.
annotation.definitionFit: An &lit: a thick creamy dressing is one of the things that can drown and ruin a salad.

entries.clue: Confuse second of judges new on bench (8)

indicatorNotes.second of: take the second letter of judges

blocks.note: a settle is a wooden bench with a high back

annotation.surface: A newly appointed judge flustered by taking a seat on the bench.
annotation.walkthrough: The bench looks like the judges' bench in court; it is an old high-backed wooden seat.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to throw someone off balance, fluster them.

entries.clue: What shows resistance Her Majesty encountered in Scotland’s over (8)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in Scotland' reads as a place, but 'in' puts the royal meeting inside the Scots word

blocks.note: o'er is the Scots and poetic form of over

annotation.surface: The Queen meets someone during a visit to Scotland.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Resistance' sounds like a rebellion against the Queen; it is electrical resistance, measured in ohms.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by function: an instrument whose reading is electrical resistance.

entries.clue: One managing river dock on limitless river (9)

indicatorNotes.limitless: RIVER loses its first and last letters

blocks.note: the Exe is a river in Devon
to dock pay is to cut it

annotation.surface: A harbour master running a dock that lies on a river.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dock' looks like a quay in this river scene; it is the verb, as in docking pay.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a senior person who runs a business.

entries.clue: Home outside of Tredegar entered by rough trespasser (8)

indicatorNotes.outside of: take the outside letters of Tredegar
indicatorNotes.entered by: to be entered by is to have something come inside, so rough goes between T and R

annotation.surface: A house on the edge of a Welsh town broken into by a rough intruder.
annotation.walkthrough: Tredegar is a town in South Wales, so 'outside of Tredegar' reads as a location; it is the instruction to take its outer letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone who enters where they have no right to be.

entries.clue: Like chicken pasty? (5)

annotation.surface: Is this pie made with chicken?
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pasty' reads as the British pie, a pastry filled with meat; it is the adjective, pale.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, of a face: pale and grey, the colour of ash.

entries.clue: Mirror put back together again without any silvering initially (8)

indicatorNotes.initially: take the first letters of any silvering

blocks.note: to reassemble is to put back together
first letters of Any Silvering, removed

annotation.surface: A broken mirror glued back together but with none of its silver backing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mirror' is a verb, to copy, not the glass the rest of the clue is about.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to mirror something is to look just like it.

entries.clue: Seconds not yet composed for final stage (6)

blocks.note: type not yet composed for printing is unset

annotation.surface: A printer racing against the clock with the last page still not typeset.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Composed' is the printing sense, type set up for a page, not calm or written.
annotation.definitionFit: A figurative sense: the evening of the day stands for the last part of anything, as in one's twilight years.

entries.clue: Bostonian patriot ditching English tea vocally for his reply (6)

indicatorNotes.ditching: to ditch is to throw away, so the English letter is thrown out
indicatorNotes.vocally: said with the voice, so we go by how the drink sounds

blocks.note: Paul Revere, the Boston silversmith of the American Revolution
the letter T is said like tea

annotation.surface: A Boston patriot throws out the English tea as his answer, a nod to the Boston Tea Party.
annotation.walkthrough: The Boston Tea Party is in the picture: patriots ditched British tea. The definition is a business-English usage.
annotation.definitionFit: A regional and business usage: to 'revert to' someone is to get back to them with an answer.

entries.clue: US outlet charges rent (9)

blocks.note: police book, or charge, an offender
rent is the past tense of rend, to tear

annotation.surface: An American shop that charges rent.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rent' looks like money paid to a landlord; it is the past tense of rend.
annotation.definitionFit: A regional use: the American word for a bookshop, a retail outlet.

entries.clue: Person lingering in large building, one holding fifty (8)

indicatorNotes.holding: to hold is to keep within, so the one keeps fifty inside it

blocks.note: a barn is a large farm building
an ace is a one in cards
L is fifty in Roman numerals

annotation.surface: Someone loitering in a great hall where someone is keeping hold of fifty.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is figurative, borrowed from the shellfish that clings to rocks and hulls.
annotation.definitionFit: A figurative sense: a hanger-on who clings to company like the shellfish to a hull.

entries.clue: Speed of pigs eating paper at first seems surprising (9)

indicatorNotes.eating: what is eaten goes inside, so the paper ends up within the pigs
indicatorNotes.at first: take the first letters of seems and surprising

annotation.surface: Pigs gobbling up a newspaper remarkably fast.
annotation.walkthrough: 'At first' serves both seems and surprising, giving two letters. The FT is the Financial Times.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the quality of being fast.

entries.clue: Atmospherically managed broadcast about health (3-11)

indicatorNotes.about: 'about' means round the outside, so broadcast wraps round health

blocks.note: a programme aired is one broadcast
condition = state of health, as in 'in good condition'

annotation.surface: A health programme put out on the radio in a controlled atmosphere.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' could be present tense; it is the past participle, which is what lets it split round the health word.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic-leaning paraphrase: a room whose atmosphere is controlled by machine.

entries.clue: Partisan evaluated involving European Judges (10)

indicatorNotes.involving: to involve is literally to roll up inside, so evaluated wraps round the rest

blocks.note: Jud is the abbreviation of the Book of Judges

annotation.surface: Complaint that a biased panel of European judges assessed the case.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Judges' is the Old Testament book, not the people on the bench.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: biased towards one side.

entries.clue: Musical piece duo plays with peril (8)

indicatorNotes.plays: to play with something is to toy with it, so the letters are moved around

annotation.surface: A musical duo performing a daring piece.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Plays' fits the musicians' world; here it tells you to rearrange the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A foreign form: the Italian name for a prelude, an introductory piece.

entries.clue: Oxygen present in mostly unpolluted stream (4)

indicatorNotes.present in: to be present in something is to be inside it

blocks.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

annotation.surface: A report on the oxygen levels of a clean river.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stream' looks like a noun, a brook; it is the verb, to flow.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym as verbs: to flow out in quantity.

entries.clue: Outstanding passage from theremin entertains (7)

indicatorNotes.passage from: a passage is a stretch of text, here lifted from the words

annotation.surface: Praise for a piece of music played on the theremin.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Passage' reads as a piece of music, fitting the theremin, an electronic instrument played without being touched.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: distinguished, standing out above others.

entries.clue: Fashionable individual’s a weak person, strangely atheistic (12)

blocks.note: a sop is a weakling, a milksop

annotation.surface: A trendy person dismissed as a wimp for oddly godless views.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's is 'has': the definition has the wordplay as its make-up.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a worldly person of refined, fashionable tastes.

entries.clue: Plaintive note on current account (7)

blocks.note: the on side in cricket is also called the leg side
I is the symbol for electric current

annotation.surface: A sad note written about a bank account.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On' is cricket: the on side, where a right-handed batter's legs point, is also the leg side.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: mournful, in the manner of an elegy.

entries.clue: Make projections of additional ring in section of earth’s crust (11)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in' puts the ring inside the crustal section

blocks.note: a tectonic plate is a section of the earth's crust

annotation.surface: A geologist's notes on an extra ring found in the earth's crust.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Projections' could be bumps on a rock in this geology scene; it means forecasts.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to project known trends forward to estimate the unknown.

entries.clue: Float purchase blocked by Oscar (4)

indicatorNotes.blocked by: a thing blocked by something has it stuck in the middle

blocks.note: Oscar is O in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: A share flotation where someone called Oscar stops the buying.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Float' suggests a stock-market flotation beside 'purchase'; it is the thing that bobs on water.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a moored marker that floats on the water.

entries.clue: Weak leader of national board is pitiful (10)

indicatorNotes.leader of: take the first letter of national

blocks.note: a lame excuse is a weak one
a board is a table, as in bed and board

annotation.surface: A verdict that a national board's weak chairman is pathetic.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Leader of national board' reads as a chairman; split it after the first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: so bad as to be deplorable.

entries.clue: Secondary route tended to be liberal (5-6)

blocks.note: a B-road is a British secondary road, below an A-road
to mind a child is to tend it

annotation.surface: A back road that tended towards liberal politics.
annotation.walkthrough: British roads are graded A, B and so on; a B-road is a minor or secondary route.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: tolerant of other views.

entries.clue: Global seminar is among the very best (5-5)

blocks.note: world = global, as in world peace

annotation.surface: A boast that an international seminar is top-notch.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a straight brochure line; the trick is only in splitting it into global and seminar.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: good enough to rank with the best anywhere on the planet.

entries.clue: Increase the risk cracking the peanut (2,3,4)

indicatorNotes.cracking: the peanut is cracked open and its letters rearranged

annotation.surface: A dare to crack a peanut, perhaps with an allergy in play.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cracking' is exactly what you do to a peanut, which hides that it is the anagram instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom from poker: raising the stake that must be put in raises the risk.

entries.clue: American nonsense is fair game (6)

blocks.note: US slang for fuss or ballyhoo
a funfair stall where you throw rings over prizes

annotation.surface: The claim that American silliness is a legitimate target.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fair game' reads as the idiom, a legitimate target; it is a game at a fair, the British sideshow of tossing rings over prizes.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: US slang for fuss and nonsense, and the British fairground ring-toss.

entries.clue: Brave men, men consuming eggs (6)

indicatorNotes.consuming: to consume is to eat, so the men take the eggs inside

annotation.surface: A tribute to brave men, and men tucking into caviar.
annotation.walkthrough: The second 'men' is the plural of he, which swallows the fish eggs; the first belongs to the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: men admired for courage.

entries.clue: Sitting in sun on the end of my outside garden (9)

indicatorNotes.on the end of: take the last letter of my
indicatorNotes.outside: 'outside' puts the sun and its added letter round the garden

annotation.surface: Someone sitting out in the sun at the far end of their garden.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sun' tempts you to write S; it must be a whole star, split after its first letter to take the garden.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: spending much time seated, inactive.

entries.clue: Righteousness over words in play in high school (8)

indicatorNotes.in: the second 'in' puts over and the words inside the school

blocks.note: an actor's lines are the words in a play

annotation.surface: A school play whose script is all about virtue.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In play' belongs with words, as an actor's script. The container instruction is the second 'in'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the state of being saintly or sacred.

entries.clue: Insect that’s metamorphosed one minute since (5)

blocks.note: I is one in Roman numerals

annotation.surface: An insect that changed form only a minute ago.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Minute' could be tiny, apt for an insect; it is the unit of time.
annotation.definitionFit: A technical term: the final adult stage an insect reaches after metamorphosis.

entries.clue: River creature seen on Wimbledon common? (7)

blocks.note: a great South American river, through Venezuela
one of the Wombles, who live under Wimbledon Common in London

annotation.surface: A water animal spotted on a London common.
annotation.walkthrough: The Wombles are furry creatures from a British children's book and TV series, living under Wimbledon Common and named after places on a map.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: the Venezuelan river, and the Womble who took its name from an atlas.

entries.clue: Naughtily suggest including one’s husband (8)

indicatorNotes.including: to include is to take in, so suggest takes the other pieces inside

blocks.note: I = one, plus the S of the possessive

annotation.surface: A cheeky hint that someone's husband might be involved.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Naughtily' reads as how the suggesting is done; it is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: mischievously, like a little imp.

entries.clue: Quietly reverse trouble and win through (7)

blocks.note: rev. is the abbreviation of reverse

annotation.surface: Advice to back out of trouble quietly and still come out on top.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Reverse' looks like an instruction to turn something round; it only gives its abbreviation, and nothing is reversed.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to succeed in the end against opposition.

entries.clue: Cuts parts off fish with its middle crooked (8)

indicatorNotes.its middle: the middle letter of the fish just named

blocks.note: to lop is to cut off branches
the ide is a freshwater fish

annotation.surface: A fishmonger trimming a fish that turns out bent in the middle.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Its middle' points back to the fish's own letters, not to any word printed in the clue.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: askew, heavier or lower on one side.

entries.clue: This part of Atlantic is about described by bay (6)

indicatorNotes.described by: to describe a circle is to draw round, so the bay draws round the rest

annotation.surface: A geography note on part of the Atlantic that lies within a bay.
annotation.walkthrough: The joke is that the answer really is a bay, off the coasts of France and Spain.
annotation.definitionFit: A proper name: the Bay of Biscay is the arm of the Atlantic between Brittany and northern Spain.

entries.clue: What may somehow result from racism petition division? (8,14)

annotation.definition: What may somehow result from racism petition division?

indicatorNotes.somehow: the letters are put together somehow

annotation.surface: A question about what a divisive petition on racism might lead to.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: a petition against racism may result in policies favouring under-represented groups.
annotation.definitionFit: An &lit: favouring under-represented groups is a possible outcome of campaigning against racism.

entries.clue: Fruit perhaps preserved primarily in beer (5)

indicatorNotes.primarily: take the first letters of perhaps and preserved
indicatorNotes.in: 'in beer' reads as the preserving liquid, but it also puts the letters inside the beer

annotation.surface: Fruit kept, perhaps, in beer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' looks like a hedge on the preserving; it is just a source of a letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the commonest orchard fruit.

entries.clue: See son with drug (4)

annotation.surface: A parent noticing their son with drugs.
annotation.walkthrough: 'See' is the verb, to notice; the son and drug are just letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to catch sight of.

entries.clue: Army group also included in proposed idea (7)

indicatorNotes.included in: what is included in something sits inside it

blocks.note: a plan is a proposed idea

annotation.surface: A military unit being written into a strategic plan.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a staff officer's memo, so the military plan looks like context rather than wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a small unit of soldiers under a lieutenant.

entries.clue: Victor, chap in pain in alpine fall (9)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in pain' sounds like suffering, but 'in' puts Victor and the chap inside the pain

blocks.note: Victor is V in the NATO alphabet
Alan is a man's name, standing for any chap

annotation.surface: A man called Victor hurt after a fall in the Alps.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fall' reads as a skier's tumble; it is snow falling.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain paraphrase: a mass of snow falling down a mountainside.

entries.clue: Flat by centre of quad in Italian city (5)

indicatorNotes.centre of: take the middle letters of quad

blocks.note: a pad is a flat, someone's home

annotation.surface: An apartment overlooking a college quadrangle in an Italian university town.
annotation.walkthrough: The city has a famous old university, so the quad fits the picture.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a university city near Venice in northern Italy.

entries.clue: Bad hotels ignored entertainment in Venetian setting (3,10)

indicatorNotes.Bad: the letters are in a bad order

annotation.surface: Poor hotels passed over in favour of a show in Venice.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer is a Gilbert and Sullivan comic opera set partly in Venice.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a comic opera whose opening act is set in Venice.

entries.clue: Popular song of the recent past (9)

blocks.note: the day before today, or loosely times just gone

annotation.surface: A hit song from not long ago.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one phrase, a recent pop hit; split it at 'of'. The song is by the Beatles.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: the Beatles song, and the day before today standing for times just gone.
